newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut t-bill issue raises 327.8 bln pounds.
newsitem.headline: Beirut t-bill issue raises 327.8 bln pounds.

text.p: Lebanon's weekly treasury bill issue of April 3 raised 327.8 billion Lebanese pounds after the Bank of Lebanon restricted sales of most bills.
The previous issue raised 426 billion pounds.
The issue posted a nominal surplus of subscription against maturity of 106 billion pounds. It raised the following amounts (in billion of pounds, previous week in brackets):

The central bank said only 14 percent of all competitive bids -- those made by Lebanese institutions -- were accepted up to the discount rate and yield for three-month bills and 16 percent for six-month bills. It was 15 percent for 12-month and 35 percent for two-year bills.

The Bank also restricted the acceptance of non-competitive bids -- those made by private individuals and foreign investors -- for three- and six-month bills. It approved only 14 percent up to the discount rate and yield for three-month bills and 16 percent for six-month bills.
However, all non-competitive bids for 12-month and 24-month bills were accepted, the Bank said.
The Lebanese pound closed at 1,545.25 to the U.S. dollar on Monday from 1,545.5 a week earlier and 1,582 a year ago.
